comments.author: robertpopa22
comments.snippet:
Fixed in `10710cc9c` — but as a guard, not as a root-cause fix, and it is worth being explicit about which one this is.

**What crashes.** `TreeListView.Expand` finishes by repainting the rows the expansion touched:

```csharp
this.RedrawItems(index, this.GetItemCount() - 1, true);
```

`index` comes from the tree model's own object map. The bound comes from the live row count. This report caught the two disagreeing by an order of magnitude — index 427 against a 41-row list — so `RedrawItems` th...

comments.snippet:
Correction to my previous comment: the suspect I named was wrong, and the repro proves it.

I claimed `Tree.RebuildChildren` was the likely source of the out-of-range index, because it removes rows and then calls `RebuildObjectMap(index)` with a non-zero start, while `RebuildObjectMap` only clears the map when it starts at zero. I wrote a test to demonstrate that — refresh a branch that has just lost all of its children, then inspect the model's row list against its object map.
